name: Ranger
summary: A wilderness hunter blending martial skill, tracking expertise, and primal magic.
flavor: Far from the bustle of cities and towns, past the hedges that shelter the most distant farms from the terrors of the wild, amid the dense-packed trees of trackless forests and across the wide-open plains, rangers keep their unending watch. They are hunters, guides, and guardians of the borderlands — equally at home stalking a monster through the deep woods and reading the signs of a coming storm.

fixed: A longbow and a quiver of 20 arrows

proficienciesGained: One skill from the ranger list
multiclassing.spellcastingNote: Add half your ranger level (rounded down) when determining shared multiclass spell slots.

spellcasting.focus: None by default; the Tasha's optional rules allow a druidic focus
spellcasting.notes: You know a fixed number of spells (see the Spells Known column) and can swap one for another whenever you gain a ranger level. Rangers have no cantrips unless they take the Druidic Warrior fighting style.

features: Favored Enemy and Natural Explorer improvements

features.name: Favored Enemy
features.description:
You have significant experience studying, tracking, hunting, and even talking to a certain type of enemy. Choose a favored enemy: aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, monstrosities, oozes, plants, or undead. Alternatively, you can select two races of humanoid.

You have advantage on Survival checks to track your favored enemies, as well as on Intelligence checks to recall information about them. You also learn one language spoken by your favored enemy. You choose an additional favored enemy at 6th and 14th level.

features.name: Favored Foe
features.description: When you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can call on your mystical bond with nature to mark the target as your favored enemy for 1 minute (concentration). The first time on each of your turns you hit the favored enemy and deal damage, you increase that damage by 1d4. The die increases to 1d6 at 6th level and 1d8 at 14th. You can use this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

features.name: Natural Explorer
features.description:
You are a master of navigating the natural world. Choose one type of favored terrain: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, or the Underdark. When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you are using a skill you're proficient in.

While travelling for an hour or more in your favored terrain, you gain these benefits: difficult terrain doesn't slow your group; your group can't become lost except by magic; you remain alert to danger even when foraging, navigating, or tracking; you can move stealthily alone at a normal pace; you find twice as much food when foraging; and you learn the exact number, size, and how long ago creatures passed through while tracking. You choose additional favored terrain at 6th and 10th level.

features.name: Deft Explorer
features.description:
You gain a series of benefits as you level, rather than terrain-specific ones.

**Canny (1st).** Choose one skill you're proficient in and gain expertise (double proficiency) with it. You also learn two languages.

**Roving (6th).** Your walking speed increases by 5 feet, and you gain a climbing speed and a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.

**Tireless (10th).** As an action, you can give yourself temporary hit points equal to 1d8 + your Wisdom modifier, a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest. Whenever you finish a short rest, your exhaustion level (if any) is decreased by 1.

features.name: Fighting Style
features.description: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. See the Fighting Styles table above for the options available to rangers.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: You have learned to use the magical essence of nature to cast spells, much as a druid does. You know two ranger spells at 2nd level and learn more as you level up (see the Spells Known column). Wisdom is your spellcasting ability.

features.name: Ranger Archetype
features.description: You choose an archetype that you strive to emulate. It grants features at 3rd, 7th, 11th, and 15th level.

features.name: Primeval Awareness
features.description: You can use your action and expend one ranger spell slot to focus your awareness on the region around you. For 1 minute per level of the slot expended, you sense whether aberrations, celestials, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, or undead are present within 1 mile (or 6 miles in your favored terrain). This doesn't reveal location or number.

features.name: Primal Awareness
features.description: You can focus your awareness through the interconnections of nature. You always have certain spells prepared, and you can cast each once per long rest without expending a slot: *speak with animals* (3rd), *beast sense* (5th), *speak with plants* (9th), *locate creature* (13th), and *commune with nature* (17th). They don't count against your spells known.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.description: Increase one ability score by 2, or two ability scores by 1 each, to a maximum of 20. Gained again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level.

features.name: Martial Versatility
features.description: Whenever you gain an Ability Score Improvement, you can replace a fighting style you know with another fighting style available to rangers.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Land's Stride
features.description: Moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed and without taking damage from thorns, spines, or similar hazards. In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement.

features.name: Hide in Plain Sight
features.description: You can spend 1 minute creating camouflage for yourself, using fresh materials. Once camouflaged, you can try to hide by pressing yourself against a solid surface that is at least as tall and wide as you. You gain a +10 bonus to Stealth checks as long as you remain there without moving or taking actions.

features.name: Nature's Veil
features.description: You can draw on the powers of nature to hide yourself. As a bonus action, you can magically become invisible, along with any equipment you carry, until the start of your next turn. You can use this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

features.name: Vanish
features.description: You can use the Hide action as a bonus action on your turn. Also, you can't be tracked by nonmagical means, unless you choose to leave a trail.

features.name: Feral Senses
features.description: You gain preternatural senses that help you fight creatures you can't see. When you attack a creature you can't see, your inability to see it doesn't impose disadvantage on your attack rolls. You are also aware of the location of any invisible creature within 30 feet, provided it isn't hidden from you and you aren't blinded or deafened.

features.name: Foe Slayer
features.description: Once on each of your turns, you can add your Wisdom modifier to the attack roll or the damage roll of an attack you make against one of your favored enemies. You can use this before or after the roll, but before the effects of the roll are determined.
